newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Bildt says hard part yet to come in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Bildt says hard part yet to come in Bosnia.

text.p: International mediator Carl Bildt said on Saturday preparations for elections in Bosnia later this month were progresssing well but that rebuilding the country afterwards would be a still harder task.
Bildt, who briefed European Union foreign ministers at a meeting in Tralee, southern Ireland, said he expected most people would accept the result of the September 14 elections.
But he said the crucial period was what would follow the vote for regional and federal assemblies.
"It is really now, after the elections, that we start to put the country together," he said, adding that the first task would be to agree a constitution for the divided country.
"That is going to be an extremely complex process," Bildt, the international community's high representative in Bosnia, told reporters.
Bildt said Ireland, the current EU President, would host a one-day conference on September 28 to win cash and manpower pledges for training a police force for post-war Bosnia.
He said some 40 countries would be invited to the talks to get pledges of support for what Western states see as a cornerstone of Bosnia's recovery from civil war.
Commanders in NATO's Implementation Force IFOR say that the job of policing the streets and settling Moslem-Serb disputes should be in the hands of a civilian police force.
Irish diplomats said they expected the Dublin government, which is not a member of NATO, to pledge to help train the police but not to supply personnel.
Bildt said a lot of give and take would be needed in the country if it was to meet the goals of the Dayton peace agreement.
"Everybody will have to lose something," he said, "but Bosnia will gain."
He reiterated his hope that the United States would remain in Bosnia with a military force after IFOR's mandate expired in December.
"It can be substantially smaller than IFOR," Bildt said of the force needed. "(But) it will have to have substantial military capabilities."
It was in America's interest. "They (the Americans) have invested a lot in Bosnia," he said.
He said negotiators were currently aiming at mid-November as the date to hold municipal elections. Elections at the local level, also due on September 14, were cancelled.
Bildt said that without local elected authorities it would be impossible for refugees to return home.

Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, host of the meeting, said the ministers had endorsed the work done by Bildt and others in Bosnia, and urged municipal elections be held as soon as possible before the end of the year.
